contents.reason: This pair gives a separate finite-law example for informative censoring and truncation; it does not claim bias or consistency results for those two estimator shortcuts.

contents.name: §1.7–1.8, p.9: left-censoring note and the classification of interval-censoring types

§2.2, pp.5–6: exponential right-censored likelihood contribution and observed exposure expression
§2.2, pp.6–8: score, information, asymptotic normal approximation, and confidence intervals for the exponential model
contents.reason: This pair proves observation likelihood contributions only; it makes no MLE distribution, asymptotic normality, test-calibration, or confidence-interval claim.

contents.name: §2.2, pp.8–9: two-group exponential comparisons and exponential regression on covariates
contents.reason: Group comparison and regression inference are not claims on this observation-scheme page; no censoring assumption is inferred from covariate adjustment.

contents.name: §2.2, pp.10–12: Weibull/Gamma likelihood discussion and piecewise-exponential likelihood/MLE
contents.reason: Parametric family and piecewise-hazard MLE calculations belong to the later survival/reliability pair, not this observation-likelihood contract.

contents.name: §2.2, pp.13–14: profile likelihood with unrestricted censoring distribution and sample code
contents.reason: The local theorem separates a parameter-distinct censor factor but does not prove profile-likelihood equivalence or provide a software procedure.

alternatives.argument: For each fixed z and entry L with S_theta(L|z)>0, conditional probability gives P(T in A | T>L,z)=K_T_theta(z,A intersect (L,infinity))/S_theta(L|z). Absolute continuity yields event density f_theta(u|z)/S_theta(L|z). A censor at u>L contributes the event survival P(T>u | T>L,z)=S_theta(u|z)/S_theta(L|z). Multiplying either conditional event-status term by the parameter-distinct censor factor leaves exactly one S_theta(L|z) denominator. The assigned proof establishes this directly in step 4.1, without using Slud's result as a premise.
